findings.evidence: This commit introduces a new metadata field `IndexInfo.GlobalIndexVersion` (new in `pkg/meta/model/index.go:256`), sets it to `GlobalIndexVersionV1` for certain new global indexes (`pkg/ddl/index.go:354`), and changes non-distinct index key encoding to prefix the handle suffix with `PartitionIDFlag`+partitionID when `GlobalIndexVersion>=V1` (`pkg/tablecodec/tablecodec.go:1259`). In the first-parent code, `decodeHandleInIndexKey` did not recognize `PartitionIDFlag` and immediately calls `codec.DecodeOne` on the key suffix; `codec.DecodeOne` errors on unknown flags (`pkg/util/codec/codec.go:1312`), so a v1 key starting with 126 would fail decoding. Because older binaries would also ignore the new JSON field, they would treat the index as legacy while encountering v1 keys on disk, causing read/write incompatibility in mixed-version scenarios.
findings.fix: Add an explicit mixed-version compatibility gate before producing `GlobalIndexVersionV1` indexes. Options: (1) refuse CREATE/ADD GLOBAL INDEX that would require v1 unless all TiDB instances report a version that supports v1 (similar pattern exists in `pkg/ddl/ddl.go:1019` for job version gating); or (2) force legacy v0 format with a warning (but then the original collision bug remains). If downgrade is supported, also add downgrade protection/documentation (v1 indexes should block downgrade or require rebuild).
findings.impact: Rolling upgrade / mixed-version cluster risk: if a v1 global index is created while any TiDB nodes still run the pre-v1 code, those nodes can’t decode non-distinct global index keys (flag 126 in key suffix) and will mis-handle index access (query errors or wrong results) and/or index maintenance (writes using legacy key format won’t match v1 keys). Downgrade risk: older versions will not understand v1 keys but will still see the index as `Global` and attempt to use it.
findings.later_fix_evidence: Checked `upstream/master` at `f0813a3696`: `pkg/ddl/index.go` still sets `GlobalIndexVersionV1` without any cluster-version gate, and `pkg/tablecodec/tablecodec.go` still encodes `PartitionIDFlag` into keys for v1; no follow-up compatibility guard was found via `git log 2f9776e8..upstream/master -- pkg/ddl/index.go pkg/tablecodec/tablecodec.go pkg/meta/model/index.go`.
findings.verify: Design-level: add a unit/integration test that simulates `infosync.GetAllServerInfo` returning at least one “old” TiDB version and assert DDL rejects (or forces legacy) when creating a global index that would need v1. Runtime-level: in a real rolling-upgrade test (old+new TiDB), run the PR’s reproduction (EXCHANGE PARTITION creating duplicate `_tidb_rowid`, then create global non-unique index) and ensure old nodes either (a) never observe v1 indexes (DDL refused), or (b) can still query correctly (if backward-compat decoding is implemented).
findings.what: Mixed-version/downgrade incompatibility: `GlobalIndexVersionV1` changes global non-distinct index key format by inserting `PartitionIDFlag`+partitionID into the key, but there is no compatibility gating to prevent creating these v1 indexes when older TiDB binaries may still be serving traffic. Older binaries would ignore the new metadata field and also cannot decode the new key suffix flag (126), risking query/index correctness during rolling upgrades or after downgrade.

subject: table: Non-clustered table non-unique global index needs partid in key, v1 (#65380)
summary: Adds `GlobalIndexVersion` to global index metadata and introduces v1 global index key encoding that includes partition ID in the key for non-clustered non-distinct global indexes (and unique-with-NULL cases) to prevent key collisions after EXCHANGE PARTITION; updates DDL backfill/DML key generation accordingly and adds tests. Main risk: lacks mixed-version/downgrade compatibility gating for the new on-disk key format.
